description: This doctoral-thesis deposit describes simulations of Swedish district-heating systems using combined heat and power, heat pumps and thermal storage to balance variable renewable electricity. It compares effects at community, regional and national scales. The provider is Svante Monie. Coverage: Coverage is Sweden at several system scales. The repository dates the thesis to 2022; simulation periods and numerical resolution require the thesis itself. Access: The depositor publishes the record and its file listing on Zenodo. Only metadata was read; the files were not downloaded. Licence and cost: The deposit states a CC-BY-4.0 licence and public access. Any separately cited input data retain their own terms. Limitations: The description is a depositor statement, not independent verification of results or reusable software. File completeness and execution remain untested. For infrastructure simulation it offers a documented study of interactions between heat demand, plant capacity, storage and electricity balancing. Related resources: For comparison, model-pandapipes covers pipe-network modelling. This thematic link does not establish use by the authors.
